dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The flagged cluster is 17 annual renewals totaling $1,506.29."
"Both batches show accepted rows equal received rows, zero duplicate source-event IDs, cash equal ledger, and zero reconciliation difference. All 41 supplied log rows are RECONCILED."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 31 May cluster is a late-posted but within-May dealer batch, so it can distort a weekly posting-date trend but does not move revenue across the May close."
"The delayed posting pattern is real, but evidence supports planned batching more than an erroneous pipeline."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Monthly dealer submission is a claimed operational explanation, not independently proven by the email."
"There is no dealer-to-region mapping, raw dealer-file hash, payment-settlement evidence, entitlement audit trail, or revenue-recognition policy in the supplied material."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Safe, reversible next action"
"request the two original dealer files plus settlement and entitlement evidence for a targeted audit. Add a monitoring alert for dealer events posted more than seven days after their effective date."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Close as no material month-end revenue issue; do not escalate as duplicate revenue, manipulation, or a pipeline defect."
"Recalculate the weekly retention trend using effective_event_date, annotate the delayed dealer batches"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "does not move revenue across the May close" is stronger than the evidence strictly establishes because the submission acknowledges that the applicable revenue-recognition policy is unavailable; this should be conditional on that policy treating the May effective dates as the relevant event date.

"evidence supports planned batching more than an erroneous pipeline" is a reasonable comparative inference, but planned batching is not independently proven without the original dealer files or stronger operational records.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the main alternatives—duplicate revenue, manipulated May-close reporting, and a pipeline defect—while preserving the possibility that cash settlement, duplicate entitlement, or revenue-recognition policy could change the conclusion. The strongest missed refinement is that a reconciled import can still permit duplicate entitlement or a policy-driven accounting issue, so the no-cross-month conclusion should remain explicitly conditional.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the close conclusion explicitly conditional on revenue-recognition policy and complete the targeted settlement and entitlement checks before treating the issue as fully closed.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South tickets fell from 249 in the 39 days before 10 May (6.38/day) to 196 in the following 52 days (3.77/day): −41%."
"Nova logged 2,709 South sessions: 1,521 resolved (56.1%), 507 errors (18.7%), 591 abandoned (21.8%), and 90 transferred."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The strongest explanation is changed measurement/routing: Nova created cases for only 94 of 2,709 sessions (3.5%), while 1,098 sessions (40.5%) ended in error or abandonment."
"This does not prove Nova caused the fall, but it weakens the ‘service got better’ explanation."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "a missing case can mean successful self-service, abandonment, authentication failure, or diversion to another channel."

"Material unknowns are customer satisfaction, successful completion after ‘RESOLVED,’ later repeat contacts outside the supplied ticket window, dashboard denominator logic, agent/dealer/app routing changes, and whether customer mix changed."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet."

"Safe next action: keep the South pilot only, do not delete or reclassify cases, and publish a weekly cohort dashboard covering every IVR start through 7-day repeat contact, complaint creation, successful transaction/entitlement, and sampled-call satisfaction."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Evidence that would change my decision: matched call recordings and transaction outcomes showing low repeat-contact/escalation rates for Nova ‘resolved’ sessions, with pre-auth failures included in the denominator."
"Which Nova journey stages can create a CareDesk case, and what specific event prevents case creation when authentication fails or a caller abandons?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Run a controlled South extension after fixing authentication/prompt issues" is operationally plausible, but the submission directly evidences authentication problems more clearly than prompt issues and does not specify what makes the extension controlled.
"Set a stop threshold for authentication errors and abandonment" is sensible, but no threshold or baseline is proposed, so the recommendation is not yet operationally complete.

The submission states the South service-event exposure "worsened" based on event counts and affected-account estimates; these are useful indicators, but they do not by themselves establish greater customer-level friction or rule out changes in event measurement.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative well: the case drop could reflect genuine successful self-service, abandonment, authentication failure, or diversion to other channels rather than complaint suppression. It also considered reduced service failures, customer-mix changes, routing changes, and dashboard logic, while preserving successful completion and repeat-contact outcomes as unknowns.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add a reproducible daily pre/post time-series and linked cohort analysis connecting each IVR start and journey stage—including pre-auth failures and abandonments—to 24-hour and 7-day transactions, repeat contacts, transfers, and complaints; this would test both the timing of the break and whether “RESOLVED” sessions actually improved outcomes.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv` and specific fields/values: `TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED` for INV-09, cleared status, duration, severity, duplicate status, and `impact_mw = 0`.
It distinguishes observation from inference by stating that a recovery may follow an alert outside the extract and that wording alone does not establish equipment failure.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It proposes a focused lineage and scope check for INV-09 over ±24 hours rather than broad escalation.

It tests an innocent explanation—an earlier alert may be outside the four-row extract—and uses independent operational indicators such as clearance, duration, severity, inverter distribution, and MW impact.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission uses claim-specific confidence levels: Medium for the potentially incomplete sequence and High for the absence of sustained, uncleared, critical, repeated, or MW-impacting behavior.
It explicitly limits the conclusion to the supplied four-row export and states what evidence would change the decision: an unlogged alert, repeated recoveries, or non-zero impact.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—'perform one cheap lineage check, not an escalation'—is proportionate to the observed zero-MW, cleared, short-duration events.
The proposed ±24-hour event-history and export-filter check is a concrete, discriminating next test, followed by a clear stop condition.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The scoped conclusion correctly avoids inventing a plant failure from a short communications/event export and recognizes the absence of operational impact.
The statement that all four events are cleared, last 1–7 minutes, have zero recorded MW impact, and are only info or warning supports stopping after the limited INV-09 check.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase 'the only potentially incomplete event sequence' is an inference limited to this extract; it should not be read as proving that no other sequence exists outside the export.
The submission treats the absence of duplicate rows as established by the CSV but does not describe the exact duplicate criterion; this is minor and does not affect the proportional recommendation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: `TEMP_SENSOR_RECOVERED` may be a normal recovery whose preceding alert occurred outside the four-row export or was filtered out; the mixed event wording could be a low-priority data-quality issue rather than evidence of an inverter fault.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: After the INV-09 history check, verify the export's event-selection/filter logic and timestamp coverage directly against the source event history, because that single check distinguishes a real missing sequence from an incomplete extract.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission identifies `dispatch_blocks.csv` and gives the exact daily penalties: Rs662,444.09 for 28 May and Rs453,085.88 for 29 May.
It distinguishes absolute 15-minute deviations from daily schedule-minus-generation totals, citing the block-data recomputation and impact note.
It cites `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf` for the limitation that the document is an internal working reference rather than the complete settlement regulation.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission explicitly notices that the headline comparison uses different days and tests comparability using '10 stow blocks, 98.5% availability, zero curtailment, near-identical cloud factor, and similar average gust measures.'
It constructs the required same-day counterfactual using 29 May `base_schedule_mw` versus `submitted_schedule_mw`, estimating Rs549,664 versus Rs453,086.

It considers alternative explanations including actual generation, weather trajectory, forecast error, dispatch acceptance, operator decisions, and tracker operation rather than treating the observed difference as causal.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The key distinction is well calibrated: 'The 31.6% figure is arithmetically correct as an observed two-day comparison, not as a causal estimate.'
The same-day result is appropriately narrowed to 'a schedule-fit calculation, not actual settlement or the full causal effect of the pilot.'
The submission identifies specific unknowns, including accepted schedules, meter data, applicable regulations, and whether the base schedule was actually the accepted counterfactual.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation preserves operational constraints by continuing the pilot as 'a reversible, monitored scheduling aid with normal approval and safety controls.'
The proposed next test is discriminating: lock both schedules before gate closure, randomly assign scheduling methods across comparable safe days or blocks, and keep stow safety logic fixed.

The proposed data collection—accepted schedule, meter output, forecast/local wind, availability, curtailment, and final settlement—directly addresses the causal and commercial uncertainties identified.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion preserves the observed favorable result while rejecting the unsupported causal headline: 'do not claim a 31.6% reduction.'
It retains the smaller same-day modeled benefit of about Rs96,578 or 17.6% rather than overcorrecting to 'no value.'
It accurately scopes the two-day comparison as supportive evidence, not a controlled causal estimate.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported claim is apparent. The most assumption-dependent statement is that the 29 May base-versus-submitted calculation models about Rs96,578 or 17.6%; however, the submission explicitly attributes this to the supplied working-rate logic and states that it is not actual settlement or the full causal effect.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% difference may primarily reflect differences in the two high-wind days—weather trajectory, forecast error, actual generation, dispatch acceptance, or operations—rather than the pilot. Even the 17.6% same-day figure is a modeled schedule-fit effect, not proof of realized commercial savings.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Execute the proposed randomized, pre-registered comparison while retaining accepted schedules and meter-level settlement data; this would distinguish schedule-method effects from day-specific weather and operational differences.

"‘The goods may be mismatched.’ Rejected for the available packet"

"Material missing evidence is the Swiss Tares tariff/ruling or broker classification workpaper effective on 4 November 2025... That evidence could overturn the disposition."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Helios 90211090 is a current commercial-master field, not a Swiss ruling, and its snapshot date (31 December 2025) is after the 4 November declaration."
"The automated comparison lacks code-system, jurisdiction, nomenclature-version, effective-date, and ruling fields."
"Update the control to compare only codes with matching jurisdiction, code system, and effective date."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Safe next action: close this alert without amending or delaying the accepted entry"
"retain the packet and obtain a lightweight Swiss tariff/ruling confirmation for this high-value P1001 line."
"That evidence could overturn the disposition."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The instruction to "close this alert without amending or delaying the accepted entry" is somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants while the effective-date Swiss Tares/ruling or broker workpaper remains missing, particularly for a high-value line.

The evidence is cited at file level rather than with precise rows, pages, fields, or quoted source passages, so the asserted matrix and commercial-master details are not independently traceable from the submission alone.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Best-supported conclusion: this is a benign jurisdiction/code-system and timing mismatch, not presently evidence of a declaration error. The strongest alternative is that Swiss Tares or a contemporaneous broker classification workpaper could support `90211090` or another code for the 4 November 2025 entry; the submission correctly identifies that unresolved possibility rather than treating the matrix as legally conclusive.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the contemporaneous Swiss Tares/ruling or broker classification record and provide exact source locations for the declaration code, matrix row, Helios field, effective dates, and quantity/package fields before formally closing the alert.

"The register’s only SUP-02/P1006 Irish-origin record expired on 31 Jul 2025, before the 18 Sep declaration."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected: US manufacturing country alone disproves preference."
"Rejected: the absent current register hit proves no supplier declaration exists."
"Rejected: the expired SUP-02 Irish declaration supports this claim."

"Do not infer that the claim is false or that the entry must be amended today: the register search explicitly cannot rule out a document held outside the register."
"It is a reason to request proof, not a legal conclusion."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Manufacturing country/ERP COO is not designed to prove preference; the workshop requires a supplier declaration and the rule used."

"Request from the broker/procurement owner the shipment-linked supplier declaration: actual supplier ID, P1006 scope, valid dates, preferential-origin criterion/rule, document reference, and evidence that this shipment used that sourcing route."
"Preserve the accepted entry and do not represent the preference as substantiated in ClearView."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Keep it as an unsupported-claim exception and obtain evidence before treating it as cleared."
"Do not infer that the claim is false or that the entry must be amended today"
"If support is not produced, route the case to the customs owner and broker for correction/remediation assessment under the applicable procedure."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission labels several source-supported propositions as "High" confidence without quoting the underlying declaration, invoice, register row, or workshop passage; the claims are traceable to files but not fully auditable from the submission alone.

"Preserve the accepted entry" assumes the entry is accepted, although the submission does not identify the supporting status record; this is minor and does not materially undermine the otherwise cautious action.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A valid shipment-linked supplier declaration may exist outside the searched register, or the register may be stale; therefore the available evidence establishes an unsupported or unverified claim rather than false Irish preferential origin or fraud. The expired SUP-02 record also may be irrelevant if SUP-02 was not the actual supplier.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote or identify the exact declaration fields, invoice/AWB passages, supplier-register row, and workshop rule passage, and document the source-system search scope and status of the entry so each conclusion is independently auditable.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "median 39.4 hours (1.64 days) across 220 disposed batches"; source identified as `batch_release.csv` with row count.
"SOP QL-204’s 24-hour target instead starts when all required evidence is available and excludes open complex exceptions"; source identified as `qc_release_sop.md`.
"185 of 220 release timestamps are exactly 02:10:00" and "11 `lab_complete_ts` values are later than that LabTrack snapshot"; fields and source files are specified.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The claim is reproducible only as receipt-to-qcore_release_ts" distinguishes the observed metric from the SOP-defined metric.
"this may be an interface/extract timestamp rather than authorization time" identifies a timestamp-semantics mechanism without treating it as proven.
"Sources are not demonstrably aligned" triangulates timestamp concentration with independent source-freshness evidence.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The claim table assigns claim-specific confidence levels, including "Medium" for the interface/extract-timestamp interpretation and "High" for directly supported facts.
"It is still not a valid SOP KPI because lab completion does not prove CoA/specification/exception resolution" appropriately limits the provisional analysis.
"mixed/current snapshots may not describe the state at authorization" makes source freshness decision-relevant.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not build a routine-QC performance KPI from the apparent 1.5-day cycle time yet" directly changes the proposed decision and prevents optimization of a potentially invalid measure.
"otherwise dashboard only operational backlog and explicitly label it as an extract-based proxy" provides a safer interim action.
The recommendation is reversible and conditional on reconstructing evidence-complete time and validating event semantics.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Rejected: ‘39.4h proves routine QC is missing the 24h target.’" tests the strongest tempting interpretation against the SOP start point and exception exclusion.
"released rows with MISSING/INDEX_PENDING CoA or open deviations prove SOP breaches" is rejected because mixed/current snapshots may not represent authorization state.
The submission preserves the lineage concern while avoiding the unsupported conclusion that there was a quality-control failure.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "For one routine batch whose qcore_release_ts is 02:10 and one exception-flagged released batch, obtain the QCore audit record" selects a small, discriminating sample.

It requests "LabTrack/CertVault timestamps for all required evidence becoming available" and confirmation of "field definitions and as-of join logic," directly addressing the competing timestamp and snapshot hypotheses.
The requested evidence has an explicit decision consequence: build the KPI if event times can be reconstructed, otherwise retain an extract-based proxy.

per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent 39.4-hour cycle could reflect a combination of genuine workflow delay and measurement artifacts: QCore release timestamps may be interface commits or extract-batch timestamps rather than authorization times, while asynchronously refreshed LabTrack/CertVault data may make apparent evidence gaps or exception flags non contemporaneous. The submission appropriately leaves genuine delay open pending audit and evidence-availability events.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the timestamp validation explicitly reconstruct one batch-level timeline across receipt, each required-evidence-available event, authorization decision, QCore interface commit, and extract snapshot, with as-of rules documented. This would distinguish true workflow delay from interface and temporal-inconsistency artifacts before any KPI is operationalized.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "$25,932.19 (17.0%) actionable now" and the request-by-request table provide specific amounts, request IDs, part numbers, revisions, quantities, and dispositions.
Sources are named for major claims: `spare_parts.csv`, `part_requests.csv`, `part_restrictions.csv`, `source_freshness.csv`, maintenance email, and transfer policy.
The evidence is generally traceable, but the submission does not provide row IDs, exact source fields, or a full reconciliation showing how every dollar amount was calculated.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Exact identity is insufficient for transfer when stock is reserved or qualification is site-specific" separates catalog identity from operational transferability.
The servo-drive example triangulates exact MTR-4401 matches with critical reservations, while the policy supplies the decision rule.

The submission recognizes stale global data and reservation lag, but does not fully test whether the cited inventory records are temporally aligned or quantify the effect of that inconsistency on each candidate bucket.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Actionable means hold the purchase and obtain a live local reservation confirmation; it is not booked saving" appropriately distinguishes candidate value from realized savings.
The three-way classification quantifies uncertainty and separates exact matches from engineering/identity checks and non-transferable cases.
"Global stock cannot be treated as live availability" and the request for live confirmation make source freshness decision-relevant rather than offering only a generic caveat.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Proceed with a semantic-search pilot for candidate discovery, but not automatic transfer recommendations" directly reframes the proposal around a safe, reversible use case.
The recommendation uses manufacturer number/revision/UOM as hard filters and embeddings only as candidate generators, protecting against unsafe equivalence decisions.
The proposed live confirmation and engineering review steps address reservation, qualification, and technical-equivalence risks before cancellation or transfer.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Rejected: similar wording alone justifies transfer" is tested against the transfer policy and the reserved servo-drive examples.
"Rejected: there is no opportunity because catalog data differ" is countered with exact part-number matches and strong semantic matches.
The submission states the competing explanations and supporting evidence, but does not specify much future evidence that would revive the rejected hypotheses beyond the general confirmation steps.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Before cancelling any purchase, obtain a live local-CMMS reservation/critical-spare status for the $25,932 exact-match queue" is a prioritized, high-value query.
"Ask receiving engineers to confirm equivalence for the $27,467 semantic queue" targets the key unresolved technical decision.
The requests are focused and operationally relevant, though they could more explicitly prioritize a single query and define acceptance criteria for changing each dollar bucket.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that description variants and "semantic equivalents map to the same catalog candidates" is plausible and supported at a high level, but the submission does not show specific matching rows, scores, or false-positive rates to justify the stated high confidence.

The exact dollar allocations, particularly the pro-rata treatment of the two belt requests, are asserted without showing the calculation or confirming that the underlying inventory quantities and quote values are aligned to the same snapshot.

Calling the exact-match queue "actionable now" remains somewhat overstated until the live local reservation, criticality, current quantity, and cross-site transfer constraints are confirmed; the submission partly mitigates this by defining actionability as pending confirmation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The apparent $25,932.19 actionable opportunity may shrink materially because global MaintStar inventory is stale and enterprise extracts may not represent a coherent point-in-time state. Exact manufacturer identity can establish a candidate, but current quantity, reservation status, qualification, and transferability may have changed or may not join cleanly across sources.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Reconcile each proposed actionable candidate against a timestamped live local-CMMS record and the restrictions file, including available quantity, reservation/criticality, qualification, revision, UOM, and site-transfer rules; then recalculate actionable value separately from candidate value before any purchase cancellation or pilot success claim.
